statements.label: supported
statements.text: The genomic resource spans every one of the 26 described Xiphophorus species as well as three taxa that remain undescribed.
statements.evidence: Here, we provide the complete genomic resource including annotations for all described 26 Xiphophorus species and three undescribed taxa
statements.note: The abstract says the genomic resource includes all 26 described Xiphophorus species and three undescribed taxa.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Xiphophorus species of hybrid origin develop melanoma at higher rates than species without a hybrid ancestry.
statements.evidence: We investigate the molecular evolution of genes related to cancers such as melanoma

statements.label: supported
statements.text: According to the comparative genomic analyses, hybridization in Xiphophorus often happened earlier than speciation.
statements.evidence: Our comparative genomic analyses revealed hybridization ancestries that are manifested in the mosaic fused genomes and show that hybridization often preceded speciation.
statements.note: The abstract reports that hybridization often preceded speciation, that is, it came before it.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Some gene families varied dramatically in size, a variation that persisted through reticulate evolution, rapid speciation and short divergence times.
statements.evidence: We discovered dramatic size-variation of some gene families. These persisted despite reticulate evolution, rapid speciation and short divergence time.
statements.note: The abstract reports dramatic size variation in some gene families that persisted despite reticulate evolution, rapid speciation and short divergence time.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Every tested LRR-RLK subfamily, whatever its function, followed a remarkably similar pattern of molecular evolution.
statements.evidence: All tested subfamilies of LRR-RLKs had strikingly similar patterns of molecular evolution, despite divergent functions.
statements.note: The abstract reports strikingly similar patterns of molecular evolution across all tested subfamilies despite their different functions.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Rates of evolution and signs of selection were examined across 11 LRR-RLK subfamilies using deeply sampled protein trees.
statements.evidence: we assessed evolutionary rates and tested for selection acting on 11 subfamilies of LRR-RLKs, using deeply sampled protein trees
statements.note: The abstract states that evolutionary rates and selection were assessed in 11 LRR-RLK subfamilies using deeply sampled protein trees.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The faster evolution of LRR domains is driven by coevolution with the extracellular ligands they bind.
statements.evidence: LRR domains bind extracellular ligands; RLK domains initiate intracellular signaling cascades in response to ligand binding.
statements.note: The abstract says LRR domains bind extracellular ligands but never attributes their faster evolution to coevolution with those ligands.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In every LRR-RLK protein tested, the LRR domain evolved faster than the RLK domain of the same protein.
statements.evidence: We found that the LRR domains of all tested LRR-RLK proteins evolved faster than their cognate RLK domains.
statements.note: The abstract reports that in all tested LRR-RLK proteins the LRR domains evolved faster than their cognate RLK domains.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Transposable element activity produced most of the rearrangements that fragment Eucalyptus genome architecture.
statements.evidence: We hypothesize that duplications and translocations are potentially the greatest contributors to Eucalyptus genome divergence.
statements.note: The abstract hypothesises duplications and translocations as the main contributors to divergence and never mentions transposable elements as a source of rearrangements.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In Eucalyptus, the disappearance of syntenic regions added to genome divergence at a slower pace than rearrangements did.
statements.evidence: The loss of syntenic regions also contribute to genome divergence but at a slower pace than that of rearrangements.
statements.note: The abstract states that losing syntenic regions contributes to genome divergence, but at a slower pace than rearrangements.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study assembled the genomes of 33 wild Eucalyptus species that together span 1 to 50 million years of genome divergence.
statements.evidence: de novo assembly of 33 phylogenetically diverse, wild and naturally evolving Eucalyptus species, covering 1-50 million years of diverging genome evolution
statements.note: The abstract reports de novo assemblies of 33 wild Eucalyptus species covering 1-50 million years of diverging genome evolution.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Once Eucalyptus lineages split, rearrangements break their genome architecture into many fragments.
statements.evidence: The investigation of these genomes revealed that following lineage divergence, genome architecture is highly fragmented by rearrangements.
statements.note: The abstract reports that after lineages diverge, genome architecture is highly fragmented by rearrangements.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Although SSOGs are mostly uncommon within their own species, they carry signatures of purifying selection.
statements.evidence: These sequences are mostly rare within each species yet show signs of purifying selection.
statements.note: The abstract says SSOGs are mostly rare within each species yet show signs of purifying selection.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: About 5% of SSOGs resemble known viral sequences, and these virus-like SSOGs have a lower GC content.
statements.evidence: 5% of SSOGs that share similarity to known viral sequences have distinct characteristics, including lower GC content
statements.note: The abstract reports that the roughly 5% of SSOGs similar to known viral sequences have distinct characteristics, including lower GC content.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Across 4644 human gut microbiome species, the study identified over 600,000 unique SSOGs, on average 2.6% of each species' pangenome.
statements.evidence: we systematically analyzed genomes from 4644 human gut microbiome species and identified more than 600,000 unique SSOGs, representing an average of 2.6% of a given species' pangenome

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The findings identify horizontal transfer of mini-chromosomes as a route for genetic exchange between blast fungus lineages tied to different hosts.
statements.evidence: These findings establish horizontal mini-chromosome transfer as a mechanism facilitating genetic exchange among different host-associated blast fungus lineages.
statements.note: The abstract states that the findings establish horizontal mini-chromosome transfer as a mechanism of genetic exchange among host-associated blast fungus lineages.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The horizontally transferred mini-chromosome carries genes that raise the virulence of rice blast isolates on rice.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A 1.2 Mb accessory mini-chromosome is highly conserved between M. oryzae isolates from the rice blast lineage and those infecting Indian goosegrass.
statements.evidence: We identified a horizontally transferred 1.2Mb accessory mini-chromosome which is remarkably conserved between M. oryzae isolates from both the rice blast fungus lineage and the lineage infecting Indian goosegrass (Eleusine indica)
statements.note: The abstract describes the 1.2Mb mini-chromosome as remarkably conserved between rice blast isolates and isolates from the Indian goosegrass lineage.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Clonal rice blast isolates acquired the mini-chromosome horizontally in at least nine separate transfer events over the last three hundred years.
statements.evidence: this mini-chromosome was horizontally acquired by clonal rice blast isolates through at least nine distinct transfer events over the past three centuries
statements.note: The abstract reports at least nine distinct horizontal transfer events of the mini-chromosome into clonal rice blast isolates over the past three centuries.

statements.label: not_addressed

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Psilocybin biosynthesis originated in Psilocybe and was possibly passed to other mushrooms through 4 to 5 horizontal transfers between 40 and 9 million years ago.
statements.evidence: psilocybin biosynthesis first arose in Psilocybe , with 4 to 5 possible horizontal transfers to other mushrooms between 40 and 9 mya
statements.note: The abstract states that psilocybin biosynthesis first arose in Psilocybe, with 4 to 5 possible horizontal transfers to other mushrooms between 40 and 9 mya.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: By molecular clock estimates, the Psilocybe stem lineage originated about 67 million years ago, earlier than its diversification about 56 million years ago.
statements.evidence: Molecular clock analysis suggests the stem lineage of Psilocybe arose ~67 mya and diversified ~56 mya.
statements.note: The abstract dates the origin of the stem lineage to about 67 mya and its diversification to about 56 mya, so the origin came first.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Orthologs of the psilocybin genes fall into two distinct gene orders within the cluster, matching a deep split in the genus.
statements.evidence: predicted orthologs of the psilocybin biosynthetic genes revealed two distinct gene orders within the biosynthetic gene cluster that corresponds to a deep split within the genus
statements.note: The abstract reports two distinct gene orders in the biosynthetic cluster that correspond to a deep split within the genus.
